shape: TypeScript monorepo: Express API, BullMQ worker, React frontend, Supabase Postgres schema, docker-compose topology.
whyThisShape: The home-field repo — the only fixture with a schema, a queue, a worker, a compose topology and a real journey graph, which is to say the only one whose shape every prompt in sectionSpecs.ts was written against. Its score is the CEILING: any property this repo cannot meet, no repo can. A large gap between this row and the others is the definition of prompt over-fitting.

knownGaps: This repo is the CEILING and it shows: 21 narration errors here against 53 on FloowForge, the same generator and the same prompts. The gap between this row and the others is the over-fitting measurement.

It is also the WORST on disclosure — 2 of 12 sections name anything the analysis could not determine, against 6 of 12 on MasterPokedex. The repo the prompts were tuned on is the one where the model feels least need to admit a limit.

All 6 architecture_deep inventory findings are the same sentence shape repeated per cluster ('It has 9 files.', 'It consists of 3 files.') — a template the prompt's 'state its real file count' instruction produces when there is nothing else to say about a cluster.
The analysed fork (KuanKongy/OnboardBuddy) lags org main, so its section list and worker structure can differ from the code in this working tree.

Analysis failed once at 98% with a Postgres 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' during record embedding, and succeeded on a plain retry. The largest fixture is the one that stresses the shared pooler.
